title: Lee considering creation of dedicated body for youth policies
snippet: President Lee Jae Myung said Saturday he is considering establishing a dedicated organization to oversee youth policies. Lee raised the idea during a ceremony to mark Youth Day at the presidential office, noting the difficulties faced by young people in the job market. "With the capabilities of current policymakers, it is difficult to emerge from this emergency situation," he said. "Opportunities for the new generation are decreasing with growing polarization and industrial restructuring due to artificial intelligence." Young job seekers have faced an increasingly tough market, with the employment rate for those aged 20 to 24 at 41.3 percent in the second quarter, compared with the 2025 average of 43.6 percent, according to government data.

title: S. Korea beats Hong Kong to begin women's handball competition

South Korea led 5-2 early and then went on an 11-2 run to blow the game wide open. Lee Won-jung led the way with nine goals and Jeon Ji-yeon chipped in eight goals. A dozen players had at least a goal for South Korea. The women's handball tournament this time will not feature a knockout stage. The top three teams among the seven in action after round-robin play will take home medals. South Korea will next play Kazakhstan on Sunday, Uzbekistan on Wednesday, China on Friday, Vietnam next Saturday and Japan on Sept. 27. Barring upsets along the way, the South Korea-Japan showdown will likely determine the gold medal. According to several federal court cases , the Sinaloa Cartel posts merchandise spotters at sea and airports to watch the trains load up with the likes of Nike shoes and electronics. title: Give the Federal Childcare Subsidy to Parents, Not Daycare
snippet: The Trump administration is drafting a rule that would let qualifying married couples draw from the existing Child Care and Development Fund when one parent stays home with the children and the other works at least 35 hours a week. The typical benefit runs about $9,000 per child each year. The change would not invent a new entitlement or demand a new appropriation from Congress. It would simply allow some families already eligible under the program’s income rules to use the money for parent-based care instead of sending it to a commercial daycare. Yet some conservatives want to kill the idea. They say any use of federal child-care money is socialism , and the only clean solution is to abolish the subsidy altogether.
